name: LEGACY archival on every rollout
description: When a rollout / deploy / new version of an asset ships (web zip uploaded, PDF re-rendered, slide deck re-exported, package re-uploaded), every superseded file in the prior source folder gets renamed with the suffix _LEGACY_pre_YYYYMMDD_rollout (rollout date, not today's date). Files with this suffix are read-only history. Never edited. Never used as deploy source.

match_any.signal: deploy artifact ships in folder X
wrangler publish / vercel deploy / netlify deploy / git push to deploy branch
PDF re-rendered, deck re-exported, .docx re-saved as deliverable

response.message:
📦 ROLLOUT ARCHIVAL REQUIRED

Detected: {rollout_event}
Folder with superseded files: {folder}

To preserve rollback safety, every prior file in that folder needs the
suffix _LEGACY_pre_{rollout_date}_rollout. I'll do this now unless you
redirect.

Files to archive: {file_list}
Rename pattern: foo.html → foo_LEGACY_pre_{rollout_date}_rollout.html

How to proceed:

  Copy the intended changes forward to a new non-LEGACY filename, or tell
  me which rollout/archive selection is wrong so I can redirect. Historical
  files are never made writable by a generic confirmation.

edit_protection.message:
⛔ ATTEMPTED EDIT ON LEGACY FILE

File: {file_path}

Files marked _LEGACY_pre_*_rollout are read-only history. They exist
so you can roll back if a deploy goes wrong. Editing them defeats
that purpose.

If you genuinely need to edit, copy to a new filename first.

why_lethal: Editing the wrong copy is one of the top causes of lost work in long multi-folder projects. The LEGACY archival convention is the single most-effective prevention across long-lived projects with multiple deploy cycles.
